activities.title: Persistent Study Task Tracker guided Build

contract.doing: Build `study-task-tracker` with `src/tasks.js`, `src/storage.js`, `src/cli.js`, `test/tasks.test.js`, `data/tasks.json`, and `package.json`. A task is exactly `{ id: number, title: string, completed: boolean }`. On success, pure functions return new arrays without changing their input. `addTask` trims the title, throws `TypeError("Task title is required.")` before mutation when it is blank, uses ID 1 for an empty list or one above the highest existing numeric ID, and appends an incomplete task. For an unknown ID, `completeTask` throws a `RangeError` whose message substitutes that ID—for example, ID 99 produces exactly `Task 99 was not found.`—before mutation; otherwise it marks only the match complete. `findTasks` performs a trimmed case-insensitive title search and returns `[]` for blank search text. Missing storage may initialize safely, but malformed existing JSON must remain untouched.
contract.why: A task tracker introduces the reliability boundaries that make a multi-file program trustworthy: pure rules, explicit storage behavior, repeatable tests, and debugger evidence. The supplied contracts prevent the learner from guessing architecture while still leaving the rule implementations to them.
contract.output: A `study-task-tracker` folder with three ESM source modules, a protected JSON data file, at least six passing built-in tests, and a debugger-backed repair note.
contract.tools: Windows, VS Code, PowerShell, Node.js LTS, node:test, and local JSON files
contract.prerequisites: Previously completed competencies: JSIN-C012, JSIN-C013, JSIN-C015, JSIN-C017. New Week concepts are taught in Core Study before this Build.
contract.finished: Module imports resolve and each file has one clear responsibility. The task operations use the exact ID, error type, error message, search, and no-mutation contracts supplied in the brief. A missing data file can initialize, but malformed existing JSON is never silently replaced. At least six meaningful tests pass with `node --test`, including exact TypeError and RangeError assertions. The debug note ties one failure to an inspected value and a verified repair.
contract.submission: Folder tree and exact run/test commands | Passing result for at least six named tests | Malformed-JSON run showing the original corrupt text was not overwritten | Debugger location, inspected value, root cause, and passing repair

steps: Create the folder structure and `package.json` with `"type": "module"`. Export `addTask`, `completeTask`, and `findTasks` from `src/tasks.js`. Copy the supplied task contract beside the functions: numeric IDs begin at 1, blank add throws the exact TypeError, unknown completion throws the exact RangeError, and every successful result is a new array.

Implement synchronous UTF-8 `loadTasks(path)` and `saveTasks(path, tasks)` in `src/storage.js`. In `loadTasks`, return `[]` only when the caught error has code `ENOENT`; rethrow every other read or parse error. Save only validated results as two-space JSON.

Use `src/cli.js` only as a small demonstration entry: load records, add or complete one supplied sample task in code, save after success, and print the resulting list. Command-line argument parsing begins next Week.

Write at least six `node:test` cases covering normal add with first/next ID, blank-title TypeError and unchanged input, completing an existing task, unknown-ID RangeError and unchanged input, case-insensitive search, and no mutation after a successful operation. Use the supplied named synchronous functions with `assert.throws`; asynchronous tests are outside this course.

Reproduce the Study debugger defect inside `findTasks`: temporarily replace the working `normalizedTitle.includes(normalizedQuery)` comparison with `normalizedTitle === normalizedQuery`, add `debugger;` immediately before that comparison, and run the Review Functions/review case with `node inspect`. Use `cont`, `watch()` or `repl`, and two `next` commands exactly as practiced; record both normalized operands and the false result. Restore `includes`, remove `debugger;`, and rerun the focused test and full suite.
Copy the data file, corrupt the working JSON, run the program, confirm the corrupt text remains unchanged, restore the valid copy, then rerun all tests.

A missing data file can initialize, but malformed existing JSON is never silently replaced.

activities.title: FoundIt CLI — Campus Lost-and-Found Manager guided Build

contract.doing: Build `foundit-cli` as the main course project. Each saved record is exactly `{ id: number, description: string, location: string, category: string, status: "open" | "claimed" }`; IDs begin at 1 and remain stable. The five commands are `add`, `list`, `search`, `claim`, and `help`. Search checks description, location, and category with trimmed case-insensitive substring matching. Keep pure item rules in `src/items.js`, the Week 7 persistence contract in `src/storage.js`, argument validation and messages in `src/cli.js`, tests in `test/items.test.js`, and a JSON array in `data/items.json`. Use the supplied command/output contract exactly so the learner and human reviewer test the same program.
contract.why: FoundIt integrates the course into a program another learner can actually run. A command contract, persistent state, focused tests, and an honest repository turn isolated exercises into one reviewable beginner project without introducing a framework.
contract.output: A GitHub repository containing a runnable FoundIt CLI with five commands, durable JSON storage, at least eight passing tests, an honest README, and recorded normal, boundary, invalid, and repaired-defect evidence.
